pedidos.pedido: F043, F044: 'Required to construct the Kinbasket, Arrow and Duncan storage reservoirs' (BC Hydro, 2026)
F045: 'an option to build Libby Dam on the Kootenai River' (USACE & BPA, 2013)
F046: 'whose reservoir Lake Koocanusa backs 42 miles into Canada' (USACE & BPA, 2013)
F047: 'more than 200,000 kilowatt years per annum of energy benefit downstream in Canada' (Protocolo de 1964)

grafias_do_espelho: MORE THAN 200,000 KILOWATT YEARS PER ANNUM… DOWNSTREAM IN CANADA (opcional)
Source: USACE & BPA, 2013; Columbia River Treaty Protocol, 1964
texto_aprovado: Canada would build three big storage dams. The United States would build the one it had asked for, Libby. Its lake backs 42 miles into Canada, and by the treaty's own count, the water it regulates makes extra power there too.

citacoes_relidas.trecho: Required to construct the Kinbasket, Arrow and Duncan storage reservoirs
helped fund the construction of the three Treaty dams in Canada
The Treaty also allowed the United States an option to build Libby Dam on the Kootenai River
whose reservoir Lake Koocanusa backs 42 miles into Canada
more than 200,000 kilowatt years per annum of energy benefit downstream in Canada
